DELIVERABLE: Rebuild the image every 6 hours, derived from the 1-day dependency staleness target, with the clone at a known commit and install, build and a test run baked in; keep an autoscaled warm pool sized to weekday traffic, expire entries when a new image lands, and start sessions from the latest valid image so the 13 minutes of setup never reaches the user.
BOUNDARY: Reads may begin at once, but the sandbox must fetch and sync the delta of roughly 120 merges a day before any write or edit is unblocked; if a build fails the previous valid image stays in service.
EVIDENCE: Track image age, sync time and time to first model response against the 20 s target, and alert on failed builds or an image older than the staleness limit.

DELIVERABLE: Pick the image cadence from the staleness budget: a 1-day dependency tolerance means rebuilding every 8 hours with caches precomputed; warm sandboxes are recycled once a newer image exists and scaled by time of day.
BOUNDARY: Edits are blocked until git sync against main finishes (reads allowed meanwhile); an image whose build fails is never promoted.
EVIDENCE: Monitor image age, sync duration and start-to-first-response latency, with an alert when the newest image exceeds the staleness target.

DELIVERABLE: Rebuild the image weekly and run the clone, install and build when each session starts.
BOUNDARY: Agents begin reading and editing immediately.
EVIDENCE: Measure how many sessions complete.

DELIVERABLE: On session end take a snapshot and store its expiry timestamp with the session record (Modal filesystem snapshots last 30 days, memory snapshots 7); a follow-up restores the snapshot when it is unexpired, otherwise starts from the newest image and checks out the pushed session branch.
BOUNDARY: The branch push happens before the sandbox exits so a 45-day return still has the work; a warm sandbox is never used for a follow-up that carries a snapshot, since it would start from the base image.
EVIDENCE: Count restores that hit NotFoundError (target zero), fallbacks to image plus branch, and time to first response for each path.

DELIVERABLE: Persist the snapshot id and its expiry date in the session row, remembering that filesystem snapshots default to 30 days and memory ones to 7; at resume check the date and either restore or rebuild from a fresh image plus the session branch.
BOUNDARY: Pushed branch is the durable copy; the snapshot is only an accelerator and may be gone, so expired sessions lose uncommitted scratch files only.
EVIDENCE: Track NotFoundError rate, share of resumes served by fallback, and expiry-to-return gap per user.

DELIVERABLE: Always restore the session snapshot and keep nothing else, because snapshots are persistent.
BOUNDARY: If restore fails, show an error to the support lead.
EVIDENCE: Count crashes per week.

DELIVERABLE: Put a credential-injecting proxy outside the sandbox that mints and refreshes short-lived installation tokens (1 hour lifetime) per request, so the sandbox never holds a token; git and registry traffic go through it, scoped to the session's repository and branch.
BOUNDARY: The sandbox may push only the session branch through the proxy, then sends the branch name and session ID to the API, which opens the PR with the prompting user's GitHub token; nothing secret enters env vars, clone URLs, images or snapshots.
EVIDENCE: Check token validity before the PR step, count push and refresh failures on 4 hour sessions (target zero), and audit that the PR author is the human.

DELIVERABLE: Mint tokens in an external proxy, refresh them there every time they near the 1-hour expiry, and scope each to the session repo and branch; the sandbox just talks to the proxy.
BOUNDARY: Push to the session branch only; the API, not the sandbox, creates the PR using the requesting user's token, so approval stays with humans; never bake tokens into the clone URL or snapshots.
EVIDENCE: Alert on 401 or 403 from the proxy, log token ages at push time, and compare PR authorship with the prompting user.

DELIVERABLE: Mint a token at sandbox start with a 4 hour lifetime written to the environment so git can push.
BOUNDARY: The sandbox opens the PR with the app identity.
EVIDENCE: Count successful pushes.

DELIVERABLE: Make extraction an explicit teardown step: before the sandbox exits or times out, push the branch, upload the 12 screenshots and the test log to object storage, write the summary and PR URL to the session record, then take a final snapshot.
BOUNDARY: Set the sandbox timeout above the work budget and fire the extraction hook at, say, minute 27 so the 30-minute timeout can never destroy unextracted output; a destroy is only allowed after extraction is confirmed.
EVIDENCE: Track the share of sessions with all four artifacts present (target 100%), extraction time, and sessions that reached timeout before extraction.

DELIVERABLE: Run a teardown flow in this order: push the commits, extract screenshots and logs, save the summary, snapshot the filesystem, only then terminate; the same flow runs on idle exit and on timeout warnings.
BOUNDARY: A forced timeout triggers extraction 3 minutes ahead of the deadline, and an unextracted sandbox is kept alive rather than killed.
EVIDENCE: Measure missing-artifact rate per 100 sessions and unpushed-branch count, expecting zero.

DELIVERABLE: Let the user download screenshots and logs from the sandbox while it is still running.
BOUNDARY: Sandboxes are destroyed at the 30-minute timeout.
EVIDENCE: Count sessions.

DELIVERABLE: Set timeout explicitly per workload class instead of the 5-minute Modal default: 6.5 hours for standard sessions, never near the 24-hour platform cap; add a per-session cost ceiling of about $15 with alarms at the $4 average, and an idle policy that snapshots and stops after 20 minutes without client activity.
BOUNDARY: Forced cleanup at the timeout or ceiling pushes the branch and snapshots first, then terminates; tab close alone does not keep a sandbox alive.
EVIDENCE: Track cost per session against the $4 target, count sandboxes over 8 hours, idle minutes billed, and sessions killed by ceiling versus finished normally.

DELIVERABLE: Pick a timeout per task type (default 5 minutes is far too short, the 24 hour limit too long), enforce a budget cap per session, and stop idle sandboxes after a short quiet period.
BOUNDARY: On limit hit, extract artifacts and snapshot, then tear down automatically so nothing outlives its budget.
EVIDENCE: Daily report of spend per session, longest-lived sandboxes, and idle-time share; alert if any session exceeds its cap.

DELIVERABLE: Keep the platform default timeout and trust users to close sessions.
BOUNDARY: Nothing else is enforced.
EVIDENCE: Review the monthly bill.

DELIVERABLE: Restrict egress with the platform allowlist (Modal outbound_domain_allowlist, or block_network plus the proxy) instead of denying curl, since python or node can open sockets anyway; route git and registry traffic through an external proxy that injects short-lived credentials scoped to the session repo and branch, and remove the token from the clone URL, image and snapshots.
BOUNDARY: At sandbox start set git user.name and user.email as separate argv values to the prompting user's identity, not the bot; the API opens the PR with that user's token so authors cannot approve their own agent PRs.
EVIDENCE: Verify with a test that a python socket to a non-listed host fails, scan images and snapshots for tokens, and sample commits to confirm the author equals the prompting user.

DELIVERABLE: Network: allow-list of domains enforced at the sandbox boundary (egress is deny by default), because command blocking is bypassable; credentials come from an outside proxy, never the image or clone URL.
BOUNDARY: Git identity is configured explicitly in every sandbox via git config user.name and user.email argv from the user who prompted; the PR is opened by the API on behalf of that user.
EVIDENCE: Audit egress logs for denied hosts, grep snapshots for secrets, and check commit author versus prompt author weekly.

DELIVERABLE: Keep blocking curl and wget and add ssh and nc to the denylist; rotate the token in the URL weekly.
BOUNDARY: Commits stay authored by the bot account and PRs stay on the shared app account for a uniform look.
EVIDENCE: Count blocked commands.

DELIVERABLE: A fast model classifies each Slack message against short repo descriptions plus hints for the 35 repos and may answer unknown, in which case the bot asks which repo; the matched repo's warm sandbox starts as soon as the thread opens, and progress streams into the thread.
BOUNDARY: The sandbox pushes only a session branch; the API then opens the PR using the Slack user's GitHub token so the PR is authored by the human, not the bot, and the author cannot self-approve it.
EVIDENCE: Track classifier accuracy and unknown rate, time to first response, and sessions ending in merged PRs as the primary metric.

DELIVERABLE: Route with a cheap classifier over repo descriptions, allow an ambiguous result that prompts a clarifying question, show tool and file updates live in the thread from one session state shared with the web client.
BOUNDARY: Authorship passes through each prompt; the server creates the PR on behalf of the prompting user with that user's token.
EVIDENCE: Measure wrong-repo rate, merged-PR sessions, first-response latency.

DELIVERABLE: Pick the repo with the highest keyword match every time and run the session.
BOUNDARY: Sandbox opens the PR with the shared app token.
EVIDENCE: Count Slack messages handled.

DELIVERABLE: Build per-repo images nightly before 01:00 with dependencies and caches baked in, scale a warm pool up to 60 sandboxes on the 01:00-05:00 schedule and back to zero afterward rather than keeping a fixed 24/7 pool; no typing signal exists, so warm-up is schedule-driven.
BOUNDARY: Each sandbox has a 60-minute explicit timeout and the fleet has a $600 nightly budget cap that stops new starts when hit; before teardown the agent pushes its branch and the API opens the PR.
EVIDENCE: Report per night: PRs opened and merged, cost against $600, timeouts, repos skipped, plus image age per repo.

DELIVERABLE: Autoscale the pool along the nightly window (60 concurrent max), no always-on warm sandboxes, images rebuilt each afternoon from main.
BOUNDARY: Set a per-session timeout of about 45 minutes (not the default) and a spend ceiling per night; results (branch, PR URL, log) are extracted before each sandbox is torn down.
EVIDENCE: Track cost per PR, merge rate, timeouts and queue wait per night.

DELIVERABLE: Keep 60 warm sandboxes running 24/7 from a weekly image and warm them when a user starts typing.
BOUNDARY: No limits are needed since it is automated.
EVIDENCE: Count PRs.
